newsitem.title: CHINA: China firms told to raise more money in securities.
newsitem.headline: China firms told to raise more money in securities.

text.p: China wants local companies to raise more money through the securities market instead of relying on bank loans, Friday's Shanghai Securities newspaper quoted a senior securities official as saying.

Most companies rely on loans by state-run banks for funds and China needs to gradually increase the amount of money raised through the market due to changing financial conditions, Zhou Daojiong, chairman of the China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC), was quoted as saying.
Zhou was speaking at the 21st annual meeting of the International Organisation of Securities Commissions (IOSCO) in Montreal, Canada, the newspaper said. The five-day meeting ends on Friday.

Zhou said China's individual bank deposits increased by an annual 33 percent, or 450 billion yuan, over the past five years but money raised through the stock market was only an annual 15 billion yuan in the past three years.
"There is a need to channel part of the bank deposits to the securities market and establish a better money-raising system for local companies," Zhou was quoted as saying.
He said the CSRC, China's top securities watchdog, would more actively explore the securities market and encourage qualified companies to raise money through the market. He did not elaborate.
The CSRC was admitted as an IOSCO member last year. The Shanghai and Shenzhen exchanges were admitted as complementary members at the current session, the newspaper said.
